Hankinnan kohteena osa-alueessa 2. on ikäihmisten yhteisöllinen asuminen. Yhteisöllisellä asumisella tarkoitetaan hyvinvointialueen järjestämää asumista esteettömässä ja turvallisessa asumisyksikössä, jossa henkilön hallinnassa on hänen tarpeitaan vastaava asunto ja jossa asukkaille on tarjolla sosiaalista kanssakäymistä edistävää toimintaa. Yhteisöllistä asumista järjestetään henkilölle, joka tarvitsee sitä sillä perusteella, että hänen toimintakykynsä on alentunut ja hoidon ja huolenpidon tarpeensa kohonnut korkean iän, sairauden, vamman tai muun vastaavaan syyn vuoksi. Yhteisöllisen asumisen palveluun kuuluu sosiaalista kanssakäymistä edistävä toiminta ja asiakkaan ohjaus. Yhteisöllisyyttä tukevana toimintana järjestetään fyysistä, psyykkistä, sosiaalista ja henkistä toimintakykyä ylläpitävää ja edistävää toimintaa, jossa on huomioitu asiakkaiden tarpeet ja toiveet. Yhteisöllinen toiminta on useimmiten ryhmämuotoista ja tukee osallistujien keskinäisiä suhteita sekä kannustaa oma-aloitteisten ryhmien muodostumiseen. Toimintaa järjestetään vaihtelevasti sisä- ja ulkotiloissa. Osallistuminen toimintaan on asiakkaalle vapaaehtoista, mutta osallistumiseen kannustetaan ja tuetaan. Palveluntuottaja vastaa, että toiminnan toteutumista seurataan ja dokumentoidaan sekä kehitetään säännöllisesti. Hankinnan kohde kuvataan tarkemmin kussakin dynaamisen puitejärjestelyn sisäisen kilpailutuksen tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa palvelukuvauksessa. Yhteisöllisen asumispalvelun hankinnan arvioitu arvo on n. 3,5 milj. euroa vuodessa. Hankintamäärät ovat arvioita eikä ne ole tilaajaa sitovia.

HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management Ltd (HAUS) is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the period 2026–2030 for the procurement of expert services related to digital transformation, innovation, governance, institutional development and public sector development. The estimated total value of procurements conducted under the DPS during its validity period is approximately EUR 40 million (excluding VAT). The DPS will be used to procure expertise for international development cooperation projects, technical assistance assignments, advisory services, capacity building initiatives, studies, evaluations and other expert services implemented globally. Assignments may be funded by, among others, the European Union, the Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland, development finance institutions and other international cooperation partners. The DPS is divided into the following categories: 1. Digital Transformation, Data, Artificial Intelligence & Cybersecurity 2. Governance, Public Sector Development & Capacity Building 3. Innovation, Investment Readiness & Technical Assistance 4. Communications, Media, Creative & Visibility Services The DPS is open to suppliers from Finland and internationally. Suppliers may apply to one or several categories and, once admitted, will have the opportunity to participate in mini-competitions launched throughout the DPS period 2026–2030. Further information regarding the scope, eligibility requirements and application process is provided in the procurement documents.

The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) is the National Plant Protection Organisation (NPPO) of Ireland. DAFM performs phytosanitary controls across the country, in a wide range of locations including farms, forests, nurseries and parks. These phytosanitary controls are in line with International Standards for Phytosanitary Measures (ISPM’s), and in compliance with the Plant Health Regulation (EU) 2016/2031, Commission Implementing Directive (EU) 2019/2072 and the Official Controls Regulation (EU) 2017/625. These controls are performed by a variety of divisions including Horticulture and Plant Health, Forestry Inspectorate, Crop Policy, Evaluation and Certification, and Import Control Operations. These controls are supported by the Plant Science Division (PSD) which performs diagnostics across bacteriology, nematology, entomology, virology, and mycology on samples resulting from Official Controls and Other Official Activities. PSD is designated as the National Reference Laboratory for all these areas including nematology, in accordance with EU regulations. Any laboratory successful in this tender will be nominated as an Official Laboratory for nematology for Ireland. DAFM undertakes a significant amount of sampling in nematology to support our agricultural industry and requires the provision of supplemental diagnostics. The successful laboratory will be expected to provide diagnostics on approximately 1500 samples across a range of matrices including soil, peat, and plant material. The diagnostics required will focus on plant parasitic and free-living nematodes, with particular focus, but not limited to, EU Quarantine and Regulated non-Quarantine species. The successful laboratory will be expected to provide results, reports, and advice within designated turnaround times and be accredited in compliance with EU regulations. The provision of this service will assist DAFM in carrying out the required phytosanitary actions to maintain Irelands high plant health status, and to protect our agricultural industry and environment.

Das Max-Planck-Institut für Biologische Intelligenz beabsichtigt 2g-Solar-Satellitentransmitter Argos PTT zu beschaffen, die satelltitengeschützt Bewegungsdaten von Vögeln übermitteln können. Diese Sender verfügen über einen Mikropower-Sender, sind solarbetrieben und verfügen über ein mikroprozessorgesteuertes Batterielade- und Energiemanagement, das es dem Sender ermöglicht, sich tagsüber aufzuladen und nachts weiter Daten zu übertragen. Ein wesentliches Kriterium ist,außerdem, dass diese Sender eine dynamisch angepasste Übertragungsrate bieten, so dass die Datenerfassungsrate bei höherer Batteriespannung steigt und bei niedriger Energieladung sinkt. Die Signale werden von der ARGOS-Bordeinheit empfangen und von dort, nach einer gewissen Verarbeitung an Bord, an das ARGOS-Bodenstationsnetz übertragen, wo unter anderem die Position des Objekts berechnet und dem Nutzer über das Internet zur Verfügung gestellt wird.

El objeto del contrato es el suministro de equipación técnica de telemetría y geocalització necesario por el proyecto “Reducing bycatch of threatened megafauna in the East Central Atlantic” (REDUCE) de la Universitat de Barcelona. El proyecto REDUCE es un proyecto europeo liderado por la Universitat de Barcelona y tiene como objetivo utilizar un enfoque científico interdisciplinario y unificar los esfuerzos de las partes interesadas para reducir las capturas accidentales de la megafauna marina por parte de las flotas europeas que operan en la región occidental del Atlántico central. El proyecto se estructura en 9 diferentes paquetes de trabajo o Work Packages. Para el correcto desarrollo del proyecto resulta indispensable la adquisición de equipación técnica especializada. En concreto, el proyecto requiere la adquisición de un amplio abanico de dispositivos de monitorización tanto en embarcaciones como en aves marinas. Incluyen GPS de varias medidas y pesos, algunos con acelerómetros, radar o receptor AIS para captar interacciones con barcos, así como modelos con alimentación solar o transmisión 4G o satelitaria que permiten seguimiento en tiempo real o de larga duración. Estos aparatos se adaptan a especies de diferentes medidas, desde paíños (pájaro de tormenta), petrels (procelaridos) hasta pardelespardelas (baldrigues), y se utilizan en contextos variados como migración, reproducción, viajes de alimentación o estudios de comportamiento al agua y en vol. En conjunto, proporcionan datos espaciales y de movimiento de alta resolución que permiten comprender mejor la ecología, el uso del hábitat y las interacciones con actividades humanas. Para el buen desarrollo del proyecto es indispensable adquirir la siguiente equipación, que tiene que permitir el marcaje y el seguimiento del movimiento de las especies estudiadas, así como la detección de posibles interacciones con embarcaciones: - GPS por embarcaciones. - GPS/GNSS ligeros para baldrigues. - Radares con alimentación solar. - GPS con transmisión 4G. - GPS con accelerometria y radar. - GPS ultra ligero con acelerómetro. - GPS/GSM con transmisión satelitaria y alimentación solar. - Fecha logger ligero. - Fecha logger compacto. - Fecha logger de medida media. También forma parte del objeto: - Suministro y recambio de componentes que estén en garantía. - Costes derivados del envío de material defectuoso hasta las instalaciones del fabricante y envío del material reparado o de sustitución de nuevo en la Universitat de Barcelona. La garantía mínima de los dispositivos será de un año a contar desde la fecha de recepción de los suministros. La contratación de estos suministros responde a la necesidad de logro de los objetivos de investigación del proyecto “Reducing bycatch of threatened megafauna in the East Central Atlantic" (REDUCE) dirigido por el Dr. Jacob González-Solís Bou, catedrático del Departamento de Biología Evolutiva, Ecología y Ciencias Ambientales de la Universitat de Barcelona. El proyecto, con Grant Agreement n.º 101135583 y financiado por la Comisión Europea HORIZON-CL6-2023-BIODIV-01 tiene como objetivo principal utilizar un enfoque científico interdisciplinario y unificar los esfuerzos de las partes interesadas para reducir la captura incidental de fauna marina e informar y promover la gestión sostenible de la pesca en el océano Atlántico central oriental. El Dr. Jacob González-Solís Bou, catedrático de Universidad adscrito al Departamento de Biología Evolutiva, Ecología y Ciencias Ambientales de la Universitat de Barcelona como investigador principal será la persona responsable del equipo investigador de la Universitat de Barcelona. La contratación mencionada tiene la consideración de contrato de suministro puesto que su objeto se encuentra comprendido en el artículo 16 de la Ley 9/2017, de 8 de noviembre, de contratos del sector público, por la que se trasponen al ordenamiento jurídico español las directivas del Parlamento Europeo y del Consejo 2014/23/UE y 2014/24/UE, de 26 de febrero de 2014 (LCSP). Lotes: Este suministro se divide en los siguientes lotes: - Lote 1: Suministro de GPS por embarcaciones. - Lote 2: Suministro de GPS/GNSS ligeros para baldrigues. - Lote 3: Suministro de radares con alimentación solar. - Lote 4: Suministro de GPS con transmisión 4G. - Lote 5: Suministro de GPS con accelerometria y radar. - Lote 6: Suministro de GPS ultra ligero con acelerómetro. - Lote 7: Suministro de GPS/GSM con transmisión satelitaria y alimentación solar. - Lote 8: Suministro de fecha logger ligero. - Lote 9: Suministro de fecha logger compacto. - Lote 10: Suministro de fecha logger de medida media. Observaciones: La unidad mínima a licitar es el lote. No hay limitaciones en cuanto al número de lotes a licitar. No hay limitaciones en cuanto al número de lotes a adjudicar a un mismo licitador. Production Mining Simulator Open Pit Excavation Simulator (top-hammer medium-heavy open pit mining simulation) The offer must consider the overall implementation of the procurement in accordance with the terms presented in the request for proposal. The tender must take into account the overall implementation of the procurement in accordance with the terms and conditions set out in the invitation to tender. If the total price of one or more simulator types exceeds the estimated price set out in the invitation to tender or other procurement documentation, the contracting entity has the right not to procure the simulator type(s) in question and allocate the funds to one or more other simulator types. 2.1 Simulator The production excavation simulator must correspond to the equipment used in mines or drilling sites in Finland and Sweden to provide students with a learning experience that mirrors real working life. The simulator must have an authentic control and management system that matches the control systems of machines used in mines. The simulator should, where possible, offer performance monitoring and evaluation to support training (e.g., accuracy, efficiency, safety). 2.2 Hardware The control devices (levers, pedals, buttons, displays) must match the controls of real mining machines, and their response must be as realistic as possible. The simulator must "understand" impossible movements and machine collisions. 2.3 Data Transfer The simulator's data transfer protocol must match that of a real mining machine and include the following topics: Importing the drilling plan to the machine's measuring device and exporting it to external memory. The open pit drilling simulator's measuring device must correspond to a modern satellite-based measuring device. Loading documentation of the drilling performance. 2.4 Software Drilling plans must be able to be designed using software commonly used in mines or machine-specific software. Compatibility of the open pit excavation simulator with realistic, practically collected satellite positioning measurement data is considered an advantage. Drilling planning software must be included in the delivery package. A license for excavation planning software must be provided to the educational institution for at least five years (from the project's end date of 30.6.2027 to at least 29.6.2032), as drilling planning is an essential part of mining education. The offer must state the validity period of the licenses to which the supplier commits. The Client commits not to use the software outside the educational institution and not to send completed mining plans to third parties. If the supplier cannot provide mining planning software, it is not necessarily a disqualifying factor if the simulator includes a sufficient number of "authentic" mining plans. The possibility of simulating fault diagnostics and error situations (troubleshooting exercises) and utilizing a mobile application and wireless data transfer is considered an advantage for the procurement package. The simulator software must be updatable with new programs. Additionally, the software must allow for monitoring learning outcomes (scenario reports from various exercises). 2.5 Displays and VR Support The simulator's display(s) must be expandable to modern display technology, enabling the creation of a realistic mining and drilling environment. A solution based solely on VR glasses use is not accepted, but the possibility of using them alongside other display technology will be considered an advantage. 2.6 Cabin The simulator with a cabin must correspond in outline to a real mining machine. The offer must state whether the simulator package includes a cabin or if it is a desktop model suitable for a classroom or another type of solution. 2.7 Maintenance and Support The supplier must provide sufficient user and maintenance training for the teaching staff and deliver comprehensive user manuals for the simulator and its software. Software updates and extensions must be available for at least five years. The availability of spare parts and maintenance must be ensured for long-term use. The offer must state the availability of spare parts. 2.8 Delivery The supplier is responsible for transporting the simulator to the purchaser (TOP Keskikatu 69, 95400 Tornio), including any transport insurance and agreements. Additionally, the simulator supplier commits to delivering software updates to ensure that the simulator meets the requirements of the mining environment well into the future as well. The offer must state the software update period in years to which the supplier commits. 2.9 Other Matters The goal of the procurement is to provide mining students with work-life-oriented mining education through situations similar to a real working environment in safe and cost-effective simulated conditions and to obtain a flexible and scalable solution for mining education needs, where physical and virtual learning support each other. In addition, the customer is willing to collaborate and partner with the supplier in other areas of developing educational environments in the mining sector. The procurement is made based on overall economic affordability (price scoring max 60 p., quality scoring max 40 p.). Offers are also evaluated based on the overall implementation of the simulators to achieve the most functional overall solution for the educational environment, serving students, teaching staff, and industry representatives, to whom mining education provides new skilled workers. Efterfrågan på avancerad materialkarakterisering inom forskningsprojekt har ökat betydligt de senaste åren. KTH och Institutionen för teknisk mekanik avser därför att stärka och modernisera sin forskningsinfrastruktur genom att upphandla ett röntgendiffraktionssystem (XRD). Systemet kommer huvudsakligen att användas för mätning av restspänningar och bestämning av halten restaustenit i ferritiska material. Det ska även kunna användas för restspänningsmätning och, där det är tillämpligt, för bestämning av restaustenithalt i andra metalliska material, exempelvis rostfria stål, höghållfasta martensitiska stål och verktygsstål. För att möta dagens och framtidens behov inom materialforskning samt säkerställa hög mätnoggrannhet, tillförlitlighet och effektivitet avser KTH att upphandla ett avancerat och automatiserat röntgendiffraktionssystem. Investeringen ska stödja såväl pågående som framtida forskningsverksamhet och stärka KTH:s kapacitet inom röntgenbaserad analys av restspänningar och restaustenit i metalliska material.
